chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Karram, from Abu Al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) passed by the Shites while they were between the Grave and the Pulpit. So I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'These are your Shites and your friends, may Allah make me your ransom.' He said: 'Where are they?' I said: 'I see them between the Grave and the Pulpit.' He said: 'Take me to them.' So he went and greeted them, then said: 'By Allah, I love your scent and your souls, so support this with piety and striving. Indeed, what is with Allah is not attained except by piety and striving. And when you follow a servant, emulate him. Indeed, by Allah, you are upon my religion and the religion of my fathers, Ibrahim and Ismail. And if these are upon the religion of those, then support this with piety and striving.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key virtues required to attain what is with Allah according to Imam Abu Abdillah?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the intimate bond between the Imams and their followers, situated historically within the sacred precincts of the Prophet's Mosque (between the Grave and the Pulpit), underscoring the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in Islamic devotion. Imam Sadiq (as) emphasizes that true adherence to the religion of Ibrahim and Ismail is not merely nominal but requires active piety (wara') and intellectual striving (ijtihad), establishing a dual criterion of spiritual purity and scholarly effort for the Shia community.
